paper_metadata.title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Models and Optimization Techniques for Financial Fraud Detection

experiments.description: Quantum Support Vector Machine evaluated on the European Credit Card Fraud dataset using PCA-reduced features and a ZZFeatureMap quantum kernel on a simulator.

problem_formulation.objective_function: Standard SVM dual optimization with quantum kernel similarity: max_alpha sum_i alpha_i - 1/2 sum_{i,j} alpha_i alpha_j y_i y_j K(x_i, x_j)
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Standard SVM constraints: sum_i alpha_i y_i = 0 and 0 <= alpha_i <= C

problem_instance.description: Binary fraud classification on the European cardholders in September 2013 credit card fraud dataset.

dataset_specification.description: 284,807 transactions; 492 fraud and 284,315 legitimate; 30 features total (28 PCA-transformed anonymized features plus Time and Amount); target Class where 1=fraud and 0=legitimate; Amount and Time normalized to [0,1] with Min-Max scaling; class imbalance handled with SMOTE and class-weighted loss; stratified split 70% train, 15% validation, 15% test; 5-fold cross-validation mentioned for robustness.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Min-Max scaling of Amount and Time; PCA reduction to 20 components; SMOTE and class-weighted loss for imbalance handling.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Majority-vote style classification via SVM decision function; evaluation with Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1, ROC-AUC, and PR-AUC.

experiments.description: Variational Quantum Classifier evaluated on the same fraud dataset using a ZZFeatureMap and RealAmplitudes ansatz optimized with COBYLA.

algorithm.variant: Variational Quantum Classifier (VQC) with COBYLA optimization

problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary cross-entropy loss over classifier probabilities: L(theta) = -(1/N) sum_i [y_i log p_i + (1-y_i) log(1-p_i)]

problem_instance.description: Binary fraud classification on the European credit card fraud dataset using PCA-reduced features.

dataset_specification.description: Same dataset and preprocessing as QSVM experiment: 284,807 transactions, 492 fraud cases, 30 features, Min-Max scaling of Amount and Time, PCA-transformed features preserved, SMOTE and class weights used, stratified 70/15/15 split.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Angle encoding of inputs; ZZFeatureMap encoding; PCA-reduced features; class imbalance handling with SMOTE and class weights.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Convert observable expectation to probability via sigmoid; threshold-based binary classification; evaluate with Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1, ROC-AUC, and PR-AUC.

experiments.description: QUBO-based hybrid ensemble that selects among QSVM, VQC, SVM, and KNN using simulated annealing and majority voting.

problem_formulation.objective_function: min_z E(z) = z^T Q z, where Q_ii = alpha * Err(h_i) + lambda and Q_ij = beta * Corr(h_i, h_j) for i != j
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Binary selection variables z_m in {0,1}; post-QUBO majority voting over selected learners

problem_instance.description: Ensemble selection/fusion problem over four fraud classifiers on the European credit card fraud dataset.

dataset_specification.description: Uses the same fraud dataset and preprocessing pipeline as the individual QSVM and VQC experiments; ensemble combines predictions from quantum and classical models after training on PCA-reduced features.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Collect predictions from QSVM, VQC, SVM, and KNN; compute classifier errors and pairwise prediction correlations to build QUBO matrix.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Select subset of learners via QUBO solution, then apply majority vote to selected models.
